beats.text: Each assistant has {voice}its own voice, and {character}its own character. And you can {change}change both.

In {settings}Settings, Voice, choose {who}who speaks. {kokoro}Kokoro, a natural voice that runs on your PC, comes first. Then {piper}Piper, with voices in many languages, and the {windows}Windows voices. They download once, and {offline}work without internet.
In {page}Voices, pick the {kokoro}Kokoro voice, {mix}mix it with another to make a new one, or add {folders}folders with voices you already have.
And choose {when}when they speak aloud: {quiet}quiet with something full screen, {night}quieter at night, and {side}sounding from the side of the screen where they are.
{profiles}Voice profiles change how they sound, with {effects}effects: {robot}classic robot, {martian}Martian, {radio}mission control, {bit}eight-bit, or just {beeps}beeps.
The built-in ones stay as they are: {duplicate}duplicate one to make your own, or press {random}New at random, and see what comes out.
In each assistant's settings, {tab}Personality is {who}what tells the AI who it is and how it talks. It comes with its package, and you can {change}change it as you like, or {reset}reset it.
Pick its {language}language, the one it answers and speaks in. And in its {voice}Voice tab, its own profile, {speed}speed and volume.
One last tip: in Voice, {try}Try it lets you type any sentence and hear it, {who}said by any of your assistants, {how}in the way you choose.
